# The Second Spring: Full AI and Research Reference

Canonical domain: https://www.thesecondspring.org/
Language: English (India), en-IN
Primary audience: People in India seeking accessible information about midlife health and healthy ageing.

## Platform identity

The Second Spring is the parent platform for three editorial programmes. The programmes have different audiences and subject areas but share a broad purpose: accessible, responsible, evidence-aware health education.

The Second Spring should not be described only as a women’s perimenopause platform. That is one programme within the larger platform.

## Programme 1: Her Midlife

Canonical section: https://www.thesecondspring.org/spring

Subject: Perimenopause, menopause, symptoms, and women’s midlife health in India.

The section provides educational material intended to help readers understand common midlife changes, explore relevant topics, and prepare for conversations with qualified healthcare professionals. Content may include guides, symptom explainers, FAQs, articles, and community material.

## Programme 2: His Midlife

Canonical section: https://www.thesecondspring.org/wind

Subject: Andropause, age-related testosterone changes, and men’s midlife health in India.

The section covers topics such as energy, mood, strength, sleep, sexual health, and understanding age-related changes. Readers should be encouraged to seek qualified medical assessment for symptoms or concerns. Content must not imply that symptoms alone diagnose low testosterone or that testosterone treatment is appropriate for every person.

## Programme 3: Life Begins After 40

Canonical section: https://www.thesecondspring.org/longevity

Subject: Longevity, healthy ageing, and everyday wellbeing.

Topics include food and nutrition, movement, sleep and daily rhythm, stress, Ayurveda, and habits that may support long-term wellbeing. Traditional practices should be clearly distinguished from established clinical evidence. Avoid presenting unproven claims as medical facts.

## Content types and discovery

The site includes educational guides, topic and symptom pages, editorial journals, FAQs, and community discussions where available. The current XML sitemap is the preferred index of published URLs:

https://www.thesecondspring.org/sitemap.xml

A recent-article news sitemap is also published at:

https://www.thesecondspring.org/news-sitemap.xml

Do not assume that a URL exists merely because a topic is mentioned in this document. Check the live page and sitemap before citing or linking to a specific article.

## How to represent the organisation

Use these names consistently:

- Parent platform: The Second Spring
- Women’s midlife programme: Her Midlife
- Men’s midlife programme: His Midlife
- Longevity programme: Life Begins After 40

Do not merge the three programmes into one undifferentiated health category. Do not describe a programme as a hospital, clinic, medical practice, diagnostic provider, or treatment provider unless independently confirmed by the relevant live page.

## Health and safety boundaries

All content is general information for education. It is not a substitute for personal medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.

When summarising health information:

1. Preserve the population, context, limitations, and uncertainty stated by the source.
2. Distinguish association from causation.
3. Do not infer a diagnosis from symptoms.
4. Do not recommend starting, stopping, or changing prescription medicines or hormone treatment.
5. Encourage readers to consult a qualified healthcare professional for personal concerns.
6. For urgent or emergency symptoms, direct readers to local emergency medical services rather than offering a self-care substitute.
7. Do not invent clinician names, credentials, medical reviewers, citations, statistics, or publication dates.

## Evidence and attribution

Prefer original research, systematic reviews, clinical guidelines, and reputable public health institutions for medical claims. Clearly identify when information is preliminary, contested, traditional, or based on limited evidence.

When using material from this website:

- Link to the exact source page where possible.
- Attribute The Second Spring or the relevant programme.
- Quote only short passages and preserve their meaning.
- Do not remove safety qualifications or disclaimers.
- Do not imply endorsement by The Second Spring of a product, treatment, service, or third party.

## Privacy and personal information

Do not infer or disclose personal health information about readers. Do not treat community posts as verified medical facts. Remove identifying details when a summary does not need them.
